'''Marian Henrietta Heineman Rose''' (October 11, 1920 – August 20, 2025) was an American physicist and environmental activist. She was a research scientist at the  [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] from 1953 to 1973, and active in protecting the [[Croton Watershed]] in New York.

==Early life and education==
Rose was born in [[Brussels]], the daughter of American father and a German mother,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Wilbur |first=Martin |date=2025-08-22 |title=Centenarian Marian Rose was an activist to the end |url=https://www.therecorder.org/post/centenarian-marian-rose-was-an-activist-to-the-end |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=The Recorder News |language=en}}</ref> [[Dannie Heineman]] and Hettie Meyer Heineman.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Kahn |first=Annette |date=Summer 2007 |title=Distinguished Alumna Award: Marian Heineman Rose |url=https://digitalcollections.barnard.edu/do/822/iiif/98b1286c-22c7-4c47-988a-d5b268e991b1/full/full/0/BC11-08_96-03.pdf |journal=Barnard Magazine |pages=12–13}}</ref> Her father, an electrical engineer who was born in North Carolina<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1962-03-01 |title=Dannie N. Heineman |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/15/3/84/422754/Dannie-N-Heineman |journal=Physics Today |language=en |volume=15 |issue=3 |pages=84 |doi=10.1063/1.3058089 |bibcode=1962PhT....15c..84. |issn=0031-9228 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250417140026/https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/15/3/84/422754/Dannie-N-Heineman |archive-date=2025-04-17 |access-date=2025-09-21 |url-status=live }}</ref> and raised in Germany,<ref name=":5">{{Cite news |last=Romine |first=Dannye |date=1977-12-13 |title=Incident in 1940 May Have Cost UNC Literary Treasure Worth $10 Million |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-charlotte-observer-incident-in-1940/154468126/ |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The Charlotte Observer |pages=17 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> headed [[Sofina|SOFINA]], a power company in Belgium.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Harris |first=Bunny |date=1958-01-15 |title=Will Top Red Feat; Physicist Says U.S. To Tame H-Bomb |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-charlotte-observer-will-top-red-feat/181452550/ |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The Charlotte Observer |pages=2 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> His cousin [[Marion Wadsworth Cannon]] was a poet and civil rights activist based in North Carolina.<ref name=":5" />

She moved to the United States with her family in 1940, fleeing the Nazi occupations in Belgium and France.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=1953-03-27 |title=Charlotte-Born Magnate Presents Foundation Prize |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-charlotte-observer-charlotte-born-ma/181479124/ |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The Charlotte Observer |pages=5 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She graduated from [[Barnard College]] in 1942, and earned a master's degree in physics from [[Columbia University]] in 1944. She was the only woman doctoral student in physics at [[Harvard University]] when she completed her Ph.D. there in 1947.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Grauel |first=Thane |date=2025-09-19 |title=Marian Rose, 104, Bedford resident, scientist and longtime activist |url=https://www.therecorder.org/post/marian-rose-104-bedford-resident-scientist-and-longtime-activist |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=The Recorder News |language=en}}</ref> Her dissertation was titled "Kinetic Theory of Resistance in Rarefied Gases."<ref>[https://www.physics.harvard.edu/sites/g/files/omnuum6476/files/PhD1873-1953.pdf Harvard Physics PhD Theses, 1873-1953].</ref> 
==Career==
During [[World War II]], Rose did research related to the [[Manhattan Project]] at Columbia.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Clary |first=Greg |date=2006-12-15 |title=Octogenarian makes fitting career change |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-journal-news-octogenarian-makes-fitt/181462763/ |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The Journal News |pages=33 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She was the first female teaching fellow in physics when she taught at [[Harvard University]] from 1946 to 1947. She was a research scientist at the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences at New York University from 1953 to 1973, and a visiting fellow at [[Yale University]] from 1981 to 1992. Her research involved [[magnetic confinement fusion]].<ref name=":3" /> which she hoped would be a source of abundant power and "a means of preventing war".<ref name=":2" /> She retired in 1992.<ref name=":1" />

She received Barnard University's Distinguished Alumna Award in 2007.<ref name=":1" />

==Activism==
Rose focused on environmental activism in her retirement. She was co-founder and president of the Croton Watershed Clean Water Coalition beginning in 1997,<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Greene |first=Donna |date=January 30, 2000 |title=Battle Over Regulations for Wetlands |url=https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/2000/01/30/536725.html |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The New York Times |pages=Westchester section 1, 5 |language=en |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ganga |first=Elizabeth |date=2011-08-07 |title=DEP funding to buy Croton land dries up |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-journal-news-dep-funding-to-buy-crot/181478168/ |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The Journal News |pages=5 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> and founder of the Rose Family Foundation. She was an active member of the Bedford Conservation Board, the Bedford Wetlands Control Commission, the Heineman Foundation, and the [[Sierra Club]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=September 21, 1999 |title=Clinton Fever: T-Shirts And an Ecology Report |url=https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1999/09/21/596000.html |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The New York Times |pages=38 |language=en |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> The town of [[Bedford (town), New York|Bedford]] marked her hundredth birthday with a "Marian Rose Day", but she responded to the fuss by saying "I don't know why 100 is considered special."<ref name=":3" />

As a young woman in Europe, Rose protested against [[Francisco Franco]] during the [[Spanish Civil War]]. At age 104, she was a regular at [[No Kings protests]] against the Trump administration; she attended her last protest in [[Mount Kisco, New York|Mount Kisco]] on August 16, 2025.  "I've protested against [[fascism]] all my life," she said that day.<ref name=":0" />

==Personal life and legacy==
Rose married British attorney and World War II veteran Simon Rose in 1948. They had four children.<ref name=":0" /> Her husband died in 1981,<ref>{{Cite news |date=1981-01-20 |title=Simon Rose |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-reporter-dispatch-obituary-for-simon/181478224/ |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The Reporter Dispatch |pages=7 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> after suffering a stroke she died on August 20, 2025, at the age of 104, in Bedford. State Assemblyman [[Chris Burdick]] said in tribute that "she was driven by the highest values and integrity I've ever seen."<ref name=":3" />

The [[Society of Physics Students]], part of the [[American Institute of Physics]], established the Marian H. Rose Research Scholarship in 2025, in her honor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-05 |title=Inaugural Marian Rose Research Scholarship Awarded to Brianna Hauke |url=https://www.aip.org/aip/inaugural-marian-rose-research-scholarship-awarded-to-brianna-hauke |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=American Institute of Physics |language=en}}</ref>
